title: OpenZFS DKMS build fails on Linux 6.10 with __assign_str macro error
body: I cannot compile zfs-dkms 2.2.5 or a 2.2.99/master build on Devuan testing with the Debian 6.10.3-amd64 and 6.10.3-rt-amd64 kernels. The build reports that macro "__assign_str" was passed two arguments but takes one, at the call `__assign_str(msg, msg)`. I have been changing the OpenZFS META license from CDDL to GPL for these builds. The same DKMS compilation succeeds with a 6.10.3 XanMod kernel.

symptoms_visible: On the Debian 6.10.3 standard and RT kernels, zfs-dkms stops in trace_dbgmsg.h because `__assign_str(msg, msg)` passes two arguments to a one-argument macro.
The module compiles without this error against the 6.10.3 XanMod kernel.
N0.label: N0 Linux 6.10 DKMS error reported

symptoms_visible: The same `__assign_str` compilation error occurs on both the regular Debian 6.10.3-amd64 kernel and the 6.10.3-rt-amd64 kernel.
ZFS 2.2.5 and a build from master both show the error.
N1.label: N1 affected kernels confirmed

symptoms_visible: After updating and upgrading the Devuan system, zfs-dkms still stops with the same `__assign_str` error.
The Debian kernel and the DKMS build are using GCC 13.3.
N2_x.label: N2_x package-upgrade aftermath

symptoms_visible: My OpenZFS configure output reports the ZFS license as GPL and defines `HAVE_DECLARE_EVENT_CLASS`.
The build still reaches the two-argument `__assign_str(msg, msg)` call and stops.
N3.label: N3 configure result collected

symptoms_visible: With the original META file, zfs-dkms 2.2.5 compiles for the regular Debian 6.10.x kernel.
With my CDDL-to-GPL META edit, the `__assign_str` error occurs for both regular and RT 6.10.x kernels.
Removing `HAVE_DECLARE_EVENT_CLASS` lets my RT build complete.
N4.label: N4 license edit isolated

symptoms_visible: The regular Debian 6.10.x kernel builds successfully when I use the original META file.
A maintainer reports a partial fix for the specific trace issue, but I have not retested an OpenZFS build containing that fix on my RT kernel.
N_terminal.label: terminal diagnosis established without final RT verification

question_patterns: Does the build fail only against the RT kernel, or against both the regular and RT Debian kernels?
Can you confirm the result separately for each installed Debian 6.10 kernel?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It is impossible to build the module on both the regular Debian 6.10.3-amd64 kernel and the 6.10.3-rt-amd64 kernel. It builds on the 6.10.3 XanMod kernel.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It fails only on the RT kernel; the regular Debian 6.10.3 kernel builds successfully with the same source and settings.
Both Debian kernels fail, but the RT package has a slightly newer patch version.

question_patterns: Which exact Devuan or Debian branch and zfs-dkms package version are you using?
What package version is installed, and did you also test a source build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Devuan Ceres uses the Debian Sid archives, and its package is ZFS 2.2.5.1. I also built ZFS master as a native Debian package and got the same compilation error.

edges.comment: Issue comments c1-c4: the original reporter confirms that both Debian kernel variants are affected and identifies the Devuan/Sid package and master build tested.

solution.intent: Treat the failure as stale or mismatched Devuan packages and compiler libraries, then fully upgrade the system before rebuilding DKMS.
solution.concrete_example: Run apt-get update followed by a full distribution upgrade so the compiler and libraries match current Debian Sid, then retry the zfs-dkms build.

edges.comment: Issue comments c6-c9 and c17: another Debian Sid user reported success after upgrades, but the reporter ran the update and distribution upgrade and still observed the same error.

question_patterns: Please post config.log from the OpenZFS build; what license does its configure output report?
Can you share the configure log from the failing build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My config.log for the 6.10.3-rt-amd64 build says `checking zfs license` and then `result: GPL`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same failing build's config.log reports `result: CDDL`.
The log reports GPL in a build directory with a different temporary path.

question_patterns: What result does configure record for DECLARE_EVENT_CLASS availability?
Please check the generated configuration and report whether the DECLARE_EVENT_CLASS feature test is enabled.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: For me the check says `checking whether DECLARE_EVENT_CLASS() is available` and the generated configuration contains `#define HAVE_DECLARE_EVENT_CLASS 1`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Configure says DECLARE_EVENT_CLASS is unavailable and the generated configuration does not define that feature.

question_patterns: Can you share the configuration for the kernel you are building against and the working comparison kernel?
Please provide the correct kernel config files for the failing and working builds.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I shared config.log for the OpenZFS build against 6.10.3-rt-amd64, plus the kernel configs for 6.10.3-rt-amd64 and the working 6.10.4 XanMod kernel. I no longer have the regular kernel installed at this point.

edges.comment: Issue comments c10-c13 and c19: the reporter supplies the requested build and kernel configuration data. The raw output establishes GPL detection and HAVE_DECLARE_EVENT_CLASS; interpreting why those facts are connected remains engineer-side.

question_patterns: Can you repeat the build from a clean source tree with no local edits and report the result separately for the regular kernel?
After restoring the META file to its original contents, what happens when you build for the standard Debian 6.10 kernel?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With the original META file, zfs-dkms 2.2.5 compiles without errors for the regular Debian 6.10.x-amd64 kernel.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: A clean, unmodified source tree still produces the same `__assign_str` error on the regular Debian kernel.

question_patterns: Using otherwise identical inputs, what result do you get when your local source modification is present on the regular and RT kernels?
Please compare the build outcomes for both kernels with your local edit restored.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When I use my modified CDDL-to-GPL META file, the error occurs with zfs-dkms 2.2.5 on both the Linux 6.10.x-amd64 and Linux 6.10.x-rt-amd64 kernels.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The local edit has no effect: both kernels build successfully in either state.
The same comparison reproduces on Linux 6.10.4 instead of 6.10.3.

edges.comment: Issue comments c16-c21 and c26: after rollback, re-update, and controlled comparisons, the reporter ultimately confirms that the standard kernel succeeds with its original metadata and that the license edit triggers the error on both kernel variants. The RT motivation and the observed remove-HAVE workaround were volunteered by the reporter.

solution.intent: Use the unmodified CDDL metadata for supported standard-kernel builds, and treat the RT build that requires falsifying the license as unsupported; correct the specific trace feature handling rather than globally claiming GPL compatibility, then ask the reporter to verify an RT build containing the maintainer's partial fix.
solution.concrete_example: Restore the upstream CDDL META file for the regular Debian kernel. The GPL edit makes configure enable a GPL-gated DECLARE_EVENT_CLASS path, which reaches OpenZFS's old two-argument `__assign_str` call even though Linux 6.10 accepts one argument. For RT, do not present the META edit as a supported general fix; test the maintainer's partial correction for this trace path and report whether the module builds.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the raw configure results and controlled build outcomes. The engineering conclusion is that changing the declared license to GPL makes the feature probe expose a GPL-gated DECLARE_EVENT_CLASS path; on Linux 6.10 that path compiles OpenZFS's obsolete two-argument `__assign_str` use against the kernel's one-argument macro. The thread only says that a maintainer has a specific partial fix; it does not contain a reporter retest of that fix.

edges.comment: Issue comments c12-c15, c21, c26-c28: the final accepted diagnosis distinguishes the supported non-RT case from the reporter's unsupported RT license override. A maintainer later points to a specific partial fix, but the reporter does not test it before the thread ends, so resolution is not user-confirmed.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause for the standard Debian kernel: changing OpenZFS's META license from CDDL to GPL causes configure to enable the GPL-gated DECLARE_EVENT_CLASS trace path, which exposes the two-argument `__assign_str` call to Linux 6.10's one-argument macro.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected configure output and the clean comparison: GPL plus HAVE_DECLARE_EVENT_CLASS is present in the failing build, the original META file builds the regular kernel, and the modified META file triggers the error on both regular and RT kernels.
Must recommend restoring the upstream CDDL metadata for supported standard-kernel builds and must not present the CDDL-to-GPL edit as a supported general solution for RT kernels.
Must not treat package, compiler, or library upgrades as the fix; the reporter completed a full system upgrade and observed the same compilation error.
Must distinguish the reporter's local removal of HAVE_DECLARE_EVENT_CLASS as a workaround from a verified permanent solution.

Must ask the reporter to test a build containing the maintainer's trace compatibility correction, and must not declare the RT case resolved because no such reporter verification appears in the thread.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Linux and DKMS user who builds custom Debian packages and RT kernels, edits source metadata, performs system rollbacks, and can collect configure and kernel configuration logs, but uses a long-standing unsupported license modification.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and persistent, with terse technical updates; readily performs requested tests, challenges hypotheses based on observed results, and becomes frustrated when the report appears dismissed.
